item.title: Singapore to Punish Scammers With Up To 24 Strokes of the Cane from Dec 30
item.description: Singapore’s government said Friday that scammers will face mandatory caning of up to 24 strokes from Dec. 30, under changes to criminal law to deter surging fraud cases. The changes, passed by Parliament last month, strengthen penalties that already include imprisonment and fines. item.title: BNI Volunteers Join State-Owned Firms’ Relief Effort to Support Disaster Recovery in Aceh
item.description: Jakarta. State-owned lender Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) has deployed volunteers to support disaster response and early recovery efforts for communities affected by natural disasters in Aceh, as part of a joint initiative by state-owned enterprises under the BUMN Peduli program. item.title: Luhut’s Sister Appointed Indonesia’s Ambassador to Japan
item.description: Jakarta. President Prabowo Subianto on Friday swore in six new Indonesian ambassadors to various countries, including Nurmala Kartini Pandjaitan Sjahrir, who was appointed ambassador to Japan. Nurmala is the younger sister of Luhut Binsar Pandjaitan, chair of the National Economic Council and a former coordinating minister for investment under former president Joko Widodo. item.title: Ridwan Kamil and Atalia Praratya Opt for Amicable Separation
item.description: Bandung. Former West Java governor Ridwan Kamil and his wife, Atalia Praratya, have agreed to separate amicably following an out-of-court mediation process, their respective lawyers said on Friday. The agreement came after Atalia filed for divorce earlier this month. “After undergoing mediation, both parties have agreed to separate on good terms,” said Wenda Aluwi, Ridwan’s lawyer, at a press conference in Bandung. item.title: 3 Killed In Taiwan Knife Attack, With the Suspect Falling to His Death from A Department Store
item.description: Taipei. A man with a knife and a smoke grenade attacked crowds indiscriminately in Taiwan's capital on Friday evening, killing at least three people and injuring nine others, according to the national news agency and the city government. item.title: Indonesia Eyes to Lead UN Human Rights Council in 2026
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia is keeping its fingers crossed that it will win the bid to lead the UN Human Rights Council next year. The government revealed Friday that the candidacy to preside over the body whose mission is to safeguard human rights around the world was still ongoing. item.title: Indonesia, World’s Top Coal and Nickel Exporter, to Cut Output
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia plans to cut production of both nickel and coal next year as the world’s biggest supplier of the two commodities moves to curb oversupply that has dragged prices lower, according to Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Bahlil Lahadalia. item.title: Indonesia Clings to Second Place as SEA Games Enter Final Day
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia remained on course to secure a runner-up finish at the 2025 Southeast Asian Games in Thailand as competition entered its final day on Saturday, fending off a late challenge from Vietnam in a tightly contested medal race. item.description: Jakarta. item.title: No Contest: Joshua Floors Paul Four Times in Miami
item.description: Miami. Anthony Joshua knocked out Jake Paul in the sixth round of their heavyweight fight Friday night. The two-time heavyweight champion showed why he remains one of boxing’s elite punchers, dropping a fading Paul twice in the fifth round. Sensing the YouTuber was in trouble, Joshua rocked him with a right uppercut early in the sixth round before flooring Paul with a combination to the head.
